_comment: BRAC pilot behavioural-gap registry. Codes are stable identifiers; descriptions are reviewer-facing English summaries. Stage C uses these as the candidate-gap registry when identifying modules from source documents. Add new gaps via the loader script (idempotent upsert by gap_code).

gaps.description: CHW failed to refer a pregnant woman or child presenting with documented danger signs to the nearest higher-level facility.
CHW referred a patient to a facility that does not provide the required level of care for the presenting condition.
CHW did not schedule or complete a required follow-up ANC visit within the WHO-recommended cadence (4 visits minimum).
CHW did not counsel the pregnant woman and family on recognising obstetric danger signs (severe headache, blurred vision, bleeding, fits, swelling, reduced fetal movement).
CHW measured blood pressure without following protocol (rest 5 min, correct cuff size, two readings, average).
CHW did not refer despite BP ≥ 140/90 with symptoms or BP ≥ 160/100 in pregnancy.
CHW did not advise the family on the next immunisation due date or check vaccination card status during a visit.
CHW did not conduct the first postnatal visit within 24 hours of delivery.
CHW did not identify or act on neonatal danger signs (poor feeding, lethargy, fever/hypothermia, fast breathing, chest indrawing, jaundice within 24h).
CHW provided incorrect or incomplete infant and young-child feeding counselling (exclusive breastfeeding 0–6m, complementary feeding from 6m, continued breastfeeding to 24m).
CHW recommended a contraceptive method inappropriate for the client's medical eligibility, breastfeeding status, or stated preferences.
CHW did not perform random or fasting blood glucose screening for an eligible adult during a household visit.
CHW did not refer a client with random blood glucose ≥ 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) or symptomatic hyperglycaemia.
CHW did not screen for TB symptoms (cough ≥2 weeks, fever, weight loss, night sweats) in an adult during routine visit.
CHW did not provide correct ORS preparation or zinc dosing (10–20 mg/day for 10–14 days) for a child with diarrhoea.
CHW completed a visit without documenting which danger signs were assessed in the SPICE app, breaking the audit trail.
